pages.text: Flux is a powder needed for $(l:metalworking/anvils#welding)Welding$() and as the catalyst of a $(l:metalworking/blast_furnace)Blast Furnace$(). Burnt to lime, it also serves glass, mortar, limewater and leather. It is carbonate stone or shell ground in a $(l:crafting/quern)Quern$().$(br2)$(thing)Borax$() is not that kind of flux: it gives $(thing)Borax Flux$(), a different powder.
Limestone, dolomite, chalk and marble grind to flux. So do scutes, clams, mollusks and the remains of shellfish.
Borax ore grinds to six pieces of $(thing)Borax Flux$(). It welds, but it does not burn to lime, and the blast furnace refuses it. Borax is also the boron of borosilicate glass.
Burnt at 840 °C, flux becomes $(thing)Lime$(): CaCO3 gives CaO and CO2, and nearly half the weight leaves as carbon dioxide. Burn it in the open.
